topic.title: Neuromorphic Vision and Sensorimotor Hardware
topic.overview: Neuromorphic vision builds sensing and control systems inspired by biological processing, often using analog circuits or event timing rather than conventional frame pipelines. The representatives connect photoreceptor arrays, motion computation, eye movements, and spike-camera reconstruction. Hardware representation choices directly determine which information is retained.
topic.whyItMatters: Event-based operation can respond quickly to changing scenes, but finite readout bandwidth and dynamic range create constraints. Algorithms and sensors need to be designed together so efficient encoding does not discard the signal needed for reliable interpretation.
topic.evolution: The collection includes adaptive motion filtering in 1987 and analog VLSI visual and oculomotor systems through the 1990s. Later work explores redundant sensing and recent time-encoded spike cameras. These examples extend biological inspiration from individual computations to integrated sensing-and-action systems, while remaining distinct from software-only spiking-network training.
openQuestions: Which temporal encodings preserve detail across very different light levels?
How should sensor-level efficiency be compared with end-to-end reconstruction and control quality?
